notes.14.1: Aper means 'boar'; the prophecy plays on the name.

nodes.text: I do not think it too curious, nor too commonplace, to set down in this fitting place a little story about Diocletian Augustus, which was given to him as an omen of his rule; my grandfather told it to me, having learned it from Diocletian himself. When, he said, Diocletian was staying at a certain inn among the Tungri in Gaul, while he was still serving in the lower ranks, and was settling the account for his daily board with a certain woman, a Druidess, and she said, “Diocletian, you are too greedy, too stingy,” Diocletian is said to have answered, in jest and not in earnest, “I shall be generous when I am emperor.” After this remark the Druidess is said to have said, “Diocletian, do not jest, for you will be emperor when you have killed Aper.”
